objections.text: The reasoning says PostgreSQL drops the final edge and returns 27 rows. The input contains 27 edges, so dropping the final edge leaves 26 result rows. The case remains a date-rounding/MAXRECURSION attack, but its stated non-error outcome does not match the values sent.
objections.resolution: A05 now states that dropping the final edge leaves 26 rows. Its edge count and MAXRECURSION outcome match the sent chain.

objections.text: The two rows for assembly 1, component 2 have the same StartDate. They violate the source table's unique key on ProductAssemblyID, ComponentID and StartDate, so this input is outside the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A06 now gives the two same-pair rows different StartDate values, so the source unique key is satisfied while the overlapping-row sum remains visible.

objections.text: The BillOfMaterials quantities 0.05 through 0.45 violate the source check requiring PerAssemblyQty >= 1.00, and product 5 has a negative StandardCost contrary to the source Product check. The diamond input is not valid source data.
objections.resolution: A11 now uses quantities 1.05 through 1.45 and nonnegative costs. The diamond satisfies the source checks and retains the grouped-sum rounding attack.

objections.text: Products 2 and 3 both use Name 'P2'. Production.Product has a case-insensitive unique key on Name, so the repeated value used to satisfy the top-ties claim cannot occur under the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A13 now gives every product a distinct name and creates its non-key tie with shared StandardCost and ListPrice values.

objections.text: Product names 'Bolt', 'BOLT' and 'bolt ' collide under the source case-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive unique key on Production.Product.Name. The input cannot be loaded into the source table with its constraints.
objections.resolution: A14 now uses distinct names and removes the impossible case-only variants. It retains empty, trailing-space, non-ASCII, emoji, and maximum-length text inputs.

objections.text: The three identical BillOfMaterials rows violate the source unique key; the negative PerAssemblyQty violates its >= 1.00 check; and the negative Product.ListPrice violates the source Product check. This overflow case is outside the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A15 now separates the same-pair rows by StartDate, uses positive quantities, and uses nonnegative product prices. It still drives SUM(decimal(8,2)) beyond the input precision.

objections.text: The 3 -> 2 row ends on 2019-12-31 but starts on 2020-01-01. That violates the source BillOfMaterials check requiring EndDate after StartDate (or NULL), so the filtered-cycle input is not valid source data.
objections.resolution: A17 now starts the expired 3 -> 2 edge on 2019-01-01, before its 2019-12-31 end date. The filtered cycle is valid source data.
